The 86 mm is the ordered plate thickness: the allowance stands inside the figure, and the pressure calculation closes on the same value, with no second margin added later. The two gasket materials are compared on temperature limit only. Pressure capacity does not separate them at the duty of the joint, and solvent resistance is not used to rank them; the comparison is confined to the one property on which they differ in service. On temperature limit, the higher-rated material is preferred. A gasket run close to its limit loses seating stress as the material ages, and the joint then leaks at a pressure the flange can otherwise hold.
